target_customer: Parents and relatives of young children
problem: Most children under 10 lack a phone, so Toymail offers plush toys that exchange voice messages with approved adults and friends.
business_model: Consumer hardware (plush toys 59 dollars preorder, 79 retail) with free app

founders.name: Gauri Nanda
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. Ubergizmo (2013) says Audry Hill co-founded the Kickstarter project; I did not open that article, so not listed as a founder.

competitors.name: ToyTalk and Hello Barbie
competitors.what: Internet connected talking doll made by ToyTalk with Mattel
competitors.funding_then: ToyTalk reported more than 31 million dollars (source date not shown)

technical_complexity.rationale: Wi-Fi connected plush with voice messaging, app and cloud, requires hardware manufacturing but standard components.

defensibility.rationale: Characters and design were differentiating, but the concept could be copied by toy makers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mattel with ToyTalk pushed a connected doll in 2015; Amazon invested via Alexa Fund instead of competing directly.

market_need_then: Company claims 95 percent of children under 10 lack a phone; Kickstarter in 2013 targeted 60000 dollars.

identity.mascot_or_character: Plush Talkies characters such as Gory the Shark, Hank the Dino and Bitsy the Bat (Digital Trends); earlier Mailmen toys designed as a cross between a mailbox and an animal

branding.brand_signature: Plush animal characters that carry voice messages
branding.community_and_virality: Appeared on Shark Tank and in TechCrunch, Engadget and Core77 coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Character led product with Kickstarter, Shark Tank and tech press coverage, but no evidence it drove sales at scale.

pivots.why: Launch of the Talkies line reported March 2016; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Toymail went from a 2013 Kickstarter to a Shark Tank deal, Amazon Alexa Fund and Verizon investment, and YC Winter 2016 with the Talkies plush line. A recap site calls it out of business but gives no date or reason, and the YC directory lists it inactive, so the cause is not public and failure factors are empty.
notes: Seed of 1.5 million is TechCrunch's total from Amazon, Verizon and angels; CB Insights shows only 230K over 9 rounds and Craft 1.6M, unreconciled. Shark Tank deal (600K for 5 percent from Sacca and Greiner) rests on a recap site and is undated. The Shark Tank recap contradicts itself about current operations. toymail.co returned HTTP 503. Competitor ToyTalk funding figure comes from an undated article.
